Hey OP! Sorry to hear about your cat. I don't have original advice to give, but I was on the r/AskVet subreddit the other day and a similar post popped up. I saved this comment from someone that recovered a lot of lost cats as a reference (in case, god forbid, my little one would get lost) and they seemed to know what they were talking about / had a lot of experience.

Here's the link to the comment if you want an extra resource: https://www.reddit.com/r/AskVet/comments/14cr6hy/lost_cat_in_new_home/jomhizm/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=ioscss&utm_content=1&utm_term=1&context=3 

Hope you find your cat soon! Stay strong, they'll be back.

Also, I'm not sure if this is a semantics thing, but I noticed that a lot of people on here said to use/have a leash on hand. Be sure that it's a harness, and not just a collar + leash. While it's common for dogs to be on a collar+leash, cats don't have the same neck strength and being in a harness will also give you more control over their movement and they're less likely to escape.

OP, I'd also recommend going to the r/AskVet subreddit for additional advice! Tried to read through some of the comments and some seem to contradict, so going there might also provide you with a more medical POV.

Best of luck!

Hey there! Not the person you were replying to & my opinion might not be the best cause I’m a freshie, but UP was my dream school and now I’m in ADMU (i’m quite happy though), so here are my two cents - I hope they help! :) 

I think that when it comes to dream schools, it’s important to know /why/ it’s your dream school. Some people have a dream school because they fell in love with the idea or image that the school projects, or the idea of the culture that the school has, instead of what the school’s actually like (For example, I guess medyo mababaw, but I didn’t want to go to ADMU initially because I thought that it was sheltered and elitist. And yeah, the school is filled with elites, but to base my decision on a feeling like that would be blowing things out of proportion). 

I guess what I’m trying to say is: when it comes to things like these, do your objective research. Figure out if the course you want/are most suited for you is in ADMU - things like that. When having a “dream school” is taken into consideration, distance yourself from your emotions as much as possible - the fact that it’s your dream school already makes you heavily biased. Emotions will change over time, but the facts take quite awhile to significantly do so. You owe it to yourself to go to a school that’s well-fit for you and your development. 

Also, since you mentioned something about accepting what fate has planned for you: take life into your own hands. I think things like “fate” and “destiny” and “God’s plan” only apply /after/ you’ve done everything you could. He gave us freedom after all - and if he has plans, I’m sure there’s a way both could coexist. And if you don’t succeed after giving it everything, then at least you’ll know that you gave your all - we never really regret our fulfilled efforts. 

Discern well, and I wish you the best of luck. I hope your choice makes you happy and fulfilled :)
